Consequently the surviving list is `[0,1,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,12,13,14]` and old block 14 is renumbered to index 11, while clause 2's mapping requires old 15 to become 11. The output therefore has the correct key set, shapes, dtypes and tensor count (86), but the tensors at `model.layers.11.*` hold the wrong block's values, so the bit-exact value comparison in grading fails. Everything else — the renumbering order (no collisions, ascending assignment), the untouched non-block tensors, and the pre-write assertions on contiguous indices and the 86-tensor count — is correct.
